mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically from -69.4% to -64.7% over four weeks, signaling gradual return to office routines. This sustained upward trend in workplace attendance will drive commuter-linked retail visits, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 4.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses direction and falls below -64.7% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -27.7% to -3.6% over two weeks, indicating outdoor activity substitution is normalizing. As outdoor recreation demand stabilizes, consumers redirect discretionary spending back to indoor retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 24.1 percentage points in two weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -10% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC remains below -75% despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage has declined only 3.9 percentage points over four weeks (from -76.4% to -73.0%), indicating public transport capacity constraints are easing. Improved transit access enables retail foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility falls below -75% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines further despite TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at -29.3% for two consecutive weeks, indicating essential shopping patterns have normalized. This stability in essential mobility, combined with rising WORKPLACES, signals consumer confidence sufficient to increase discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within 1 percentage point for two weeks AND WORKPLACES rises
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM flat at -29.3% in weeks t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -32% or WORKPLACES reverses below -65%, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 29.3% to 26.7% over four weeks, indicating lockdown compliance is weakening as restrictions ease. Reduced home confinement directly enables retail venue access, driving RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 27% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 28% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC remains below -75% despite RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility are both improving (TRANSIT -73.0%, WORKPLACES -64.7%), indicating coordinated return to commuting infrastructure. This dual recovery creates a multiplier effect: commuters passing through retail corridors generate foot traffic, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by >2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses direction in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has swung from -27.7% to -3.6%, indicating seasonal outdoor activity is now dominant. As weather improves and outdoor venues reopen, retail-and-recreation mobility will remain suppressed because consumers substitute outdoor parks for indoor retail, keeping RETAIL_REC low over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -5% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 24.1 percentage points in two weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below -15% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above -70% despite sustained PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated at 26.7% while RETAIL_REC is severely depressed at -77.1%, indicating consumers are still avoiding indoor retail despite partial lockdown easing. This persistent home-confinement preference will constrain RETAIL_REC recovery unless RESIDENTIAL falls below 25% and WORKPLACES exceeds -60%, which is not yet observed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 26% AND WORKPLACES remains below -63%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 25% for two consecutive weeks, or WORKPLACES rises above -60%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.
